long_biography.plain_text:
Salmon's commercial instincts formed early, after his father died when he was 12 and he took newspaper-selling jobs to help gain financial independence. While undertaking an engineering cadetship, he co-founded a lighting-and-sound venture with his brother in the family garage. He ultimately bought his brother out and developed the operation into Dynalite, Lightmoves and Nightclubs Australia, later rescuing and selling the businesses after their corporate parent failed.

In 1993, Salmon bought his first Sydney pub before the Olympic redevelopment transformed Homebush. A portfolio of hotels followed, together with property projects and the education platform Skwirk. Today he is chief executive of Coho Property, pursuing residential and mixed-use developments around Port Stephens. His parallel career in motorsport stretched from rallying into Australian GT competition, reflecting a taste for operating across very different fields.
